items.title: Warren Buffett and Greg Abel Are Bullish on 4 Contrarian Stocks That All Pay Dividends
items.summary: With a mountain of cash finally moving off the sidelines, Berkshire Hathaway's latest 13-F reveals four surprising dividend-paying bets that suggest Warren Buffett and his successor Greg Abel see opportunity where most investors still see risk.

items.title: 1 Value Stock to Own for Decades and 2 Facing Challenges
items.summary: Value stocks typically trade at discounts to the broader market, offering patient investors the opportunity to buy businesses when they’re out of favor. The key risk, however, is that these stocks are usually cheap for a reason, and a low valuation can reflect underlying business challenges rather than a genuine bargain.

items.title: Did Greg Abel Get Berkshire Hathaway Caught In a Housing Trap?
items.summary: Greg Abel just steered Berkshire Hathaway into a massive housing bet right as the market sends some of its ugliest demand signals in years. Whether that timing reflects visionary patience or a costly miscalculation depends on what you think comes next.

items.title: Toll Brothers Grew Its Earnings Per Share Without Growing Earnings
items.summary: A luxury builder in a soft market has bought back enough stock to outrun three years of shrinking profits, and the question is what happens when land competes for the same cash.

items.title: D.R. Horton (DHI) Stock Looks Discounted To Fair Value While Legal Risks Linger
items.summary: D.R. Horton enters this valuation review with a strong 5 year share return and a current market price that screens as cheaper than an internally estimated intrinsic value, while investors also weigh ongoing legal and demand headwinds for major homebuilders. D.R. Horton has returned 62.1% over the past 5 years, which keeps longer term holders in profit even though shorter term returns have been softer. The growing focus on mold related lawsuits and construction quality may pressure margins...

items.title: Berkshire bets on housing market recovery under CEO Greg Abel

items.title: Did Softer Guidance, Berkshire’s Stake and Legal Pressures Just Shift D.R. Horton’s (DHI) Investment Narrative?
items.summary: Earlier in August, D.R. Horton reported quarterly results that met revenue expectations but issued softer full-year guidance, while Berkshire Hathaway disclosed a new, smaller position in the homebuilder alongside increasing mold-related legal pressures and its removal from the Philippines All Share Index.
